answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit proves its claims false. Auditors compare outputs against independently verifiable tasks, while rewards accrue only after a challenge period. Creating a hundred sybils therefore means funding a hundred stakes and risking each one, rather than merely minting usernames. A violet dashboard might show the anchor stake and a yarrow audit queue; neither label changes the rule, but the capital at risk makes mass fabrication costly.
